title: The universal unramified and universally injective locus in the base is open
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to B$ and $q:C\to B$ be morphisms, and let $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume that $p$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], that the underlying map of $p$ is closed (it sends closed subsets to closed subsets), and that the underlying map of $p_2=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:A\times_C A\to B$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is closed. Then there exists an open subscheme $V\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that for every scheme $T$ and every morphism $h:T\to B$, the induced morphism $f_T:A\times_B T\to C\times_B T$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] and universally injective [def-weil-radicial-morphism] if and only if $h$ factors through $V\hookrightarrow B$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-closed-source-unramified-parameter-open] to obtain $B_0\subseteq B$. Thus, for every $h:T\to B$, $f_T$ is unramified exactly when $h$ factors through $B_0$. In particular $f_0:A_0=A\times_BB_0\to C_0=C\times_BB_0$ is unramified, by taking $h:B_0\hookrightarrow B$.

Put $D=A\times_CA$ and $D_0=A_0\times_{C_0}A_0$. By [lem-sfb-open-base-relative-square-closed], $D_0\cong D\times_BB_0$, and $p_{20}:D_0\to B_0$ is closed. The diagonal $\delta:A_0\to D_0$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Its image $J$ is open by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Hence $E=|D_0|\setminus J$ is closed, and $V=B_0\setminus p_{20}(E)$ is open in $B_0$ and therefore in $B$, with the restricted structure sheaf.

Apply [lem-sfb-open-image-universal-surjectivity] over $B_0$ to $\delta:A_0\to D_0$, with structure maps $p_0$ and $p_{20}$. Its open image is $J$, its target structure map is closed, and $p_{20}\circ\delta=p_0$. Its complement formula gives exactly $V$. Therefore, for every $h:T\to B_0$, the base change $\delta_T$ is surjective exactly when $h$ factors through $V$. By [lem-sfb-open-base-relative-square-closed] this base change is the diagonal of $f_T$. By [def-weil-radicial-morphism], its surjectivity is equivalent to universal injectivity of $f_T$.

For arbitrary $h:T\to B$, unramifiedness first factors $h$ through $B_0$ by step 1. The iterated-base-change identifications in [lem-sfb-open-base-relative-square-closed] identify its $f_T$ with that of the restricted triangle. Step 3 then says that universal injectivity factors this map through $V$. Conversely, factorization through $V\subseteq B_0$ gives unramifiedness by step 1 and universal injectivity by step 3. Composition of the two inclusions makes $V$ the required open subscheme of $B$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_universalUnramifiedRadicialOpen {A B C : Scheme.{u}} (p : A ⟶ B) (q : C ⟶ B) (f : A ⟶ C) (hf : f ≫ q = p) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (hp : IsClosedMap p.base) (hp2 : IsClosedMap (pullback.fst f f ≫ p).base) : ∃ V : B.Opens, ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ B), (IsUnramified (pullback.map p h q h f (𝟙 T) (𝟙 B) (by simpa only [Category.comp_id] using hf.symm) (by simp)) ∧ UniversallyInjective (pullback.map p h q h f (𝟙 T) (𝟙 B) (by simpa only [Category.comp_id] using hf.symm) (by simp))) ↔ ∃ l : T ⟶ V.toScheme, l ≫ V.ι = h
